title: Protocol to develop a microfluidic human corneal barrier-on-a-chip to evaluate the corneal epithelial wound repair process
protocol: Prepare a degassed mixture of PDMS silicone elastomer base and curing agent for replica molding.
Place an empty disposable plastic cup on a scale with appropriate precision.
Pour silicone elastomer base and curing agent in a 10:1 (base: curing agent) weight ratio into the cup.
Mix silicone elastomer base and curing agent vigorously by hand using a disposable plastic fork for 5 min until PDMS appears white.
Place the cup containing the PDMS mixture in a vacuum desiccator for 30 min.
Remove the cup from the chamber to complete degassing.
Attach a master silicon wafer with desired microfabricated channel features to the bottom surface of a Petri dish (100 mm) using double-sided tape.
Use compressed filtered air to gently blow off dust particles from the silicon master.
Pour 20 g of degassed 10:1 (wt/wt, prepolymer:curing agent) PDMS mixture onto the upper layer master.
Pour 10 g of degassed 10:1 PDMS mixture onto the cleaned master of the lower layer.
Place the Petri dish with PDMS in a vacuum chamber to degas for 10 min and then on a level surface for 1 h.
Cover the Petri dish with a lid and put it in an oven at 80°C for 4 h to fully cure PDMS.
Remove the dish from the oven and allow it to cool to 22°C.
Cut the fully cured PDMS along the edge of the silicon wafer using a scalpel and carefully peel it off.
Make holes through the PDMS slab using hole punchers.
Use a 1-mm puncher to make holes through the PDMS slabs, providing access to the central upper and lower cell culture microchannels, respectively.
Use a 6-mm puncher to create the “Culture zone” and the “TEER zone”, respectively.
Put magic tape on both sides of the PDMS block and then peel the tape off to clean the surfaces.
Peel the magic tape from the lower microchannel slab.
Treat the lower PDMS surface and a coverslip with plasma for 1 min.
Place the lower microchannel slab attached to a coverslip.
Treat the porous membrane surface with plasma for 1 min.
Place the porous membrane surface attached to the lower microchannel slab.
Remove the magic tape from the upper microchannel slab and expose the channel side to plasma for 1 min.
Overlay the upper microchannel slab on the membrane.
Press down the upper PDMS slab to eliminate trapped air pockets and ensure firm contact between layers.
Insert the blunt needles into the four ports of the side microchambers.
Cut four pieces of silicone tubing to a length of 8 cm and connect them to the free ends of the needles.
Mix 5 min epoxy on a clean surface and apply it around each needle.
Wait for 30 min to allow the applied epoxy to set.
Transfer the chip into a biosafety cabinet.
Irradiate the chip with UV light for 30 min for sterilization.
Add 100 μL of phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) to the chip’s upper and lower inlets.
Add 50 μL of PBS to the middle chamber of the chip.
Perform dynamic processing on a shaker for 5 min, with a rocking angle of at least 30 degrees.
Dilute collagen solution to 10 μg/cm² with a sterile diluting solution.
Add 40 μL of diluted collagen solution to the upper and lower layers of the chip, respectively.
Add 20 μL of diluted collagen solution to the middle chamber.
Allow the chip to coat in a 37°C, 5% CO₂ incubator for 2 h.
Transfer the chip into a biosafety cabinet.
Aspirate any remaining collagen solution from the chip and air-dry for 30 min.
Rinse once with Complete Medium.
Seal the chips with parafilm to avoid collagen from drying out if storing at 4°C for later use.
Discard the supernatant and wash the cells with PBS three times.
Add 1 mL of 0.25% EDTA-Trypsin into the flask of HCEnd cells (at least 90% confluency).
Transfer the flask into an incubator at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 2 min.
Add 3 mL of Prigrow I Complete Medium to stop digestion.
Transfer the flask’s content into a 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the tube at 200 × g for 5 min.
Count the cells and adjust the concentration of the cell suspension to 5 × 10^5 cells/mL.
Add 20 μL of Prigrow I Complete Medium to the middle chamber.
Add 20 μL of HCEnd cells suspension in the lower inlet channel.
Transfer the inverted chip into a horizontal position in the incubator at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 24 h.
Discard the supernatant and wash the cells with PBS three times.
Add 1 mL of 0.25% EDTA-Trypsin into the flask of HCEpi cells (at least 90% confluency).
Transfer the flask into an incubator at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 2 min.
Add 3 mL of DMEM/F12 Complete Medium to stop digestion.
Transfer the flask’s content into a 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the tube at 200 × g for 5 min.
Count the cells and adjust the concentration of the cell suspension to 3 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Aspirate the medium from the lower outlet.
Refresh with 100 μL pre-warmed Prigrow I Complete Medium in the lower channel.
Add 20 μL of HCEpi cells suspension in the upper hole.
Transfer the chip to the incubator at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 24 h.
Do not move the chip until the next medium change (24 h later).
Aspirate the culture medium from the upper hole once cells have proliferated on the membrane.
Introduce air into the epithelial compartment to create an air-liquid interface.
Mix DMEM/F12 Complete Medium and Prigrow I Complete Medium in a 1:1 ratio for the lower channels.
Maintain continuous flow condition at a volumetric flow rate of 100 μL/h using a programmable low-pressure syringe pump.
Maintain above conditions for 14 days to allow HCEpi cells to grow and form a stratified epithelium.
Sterilize the Millicell-electrical resistance system with 75% ethanol.
Place the sterilized Millicell-ERS into the biosafety cabinet.
Connect the probe to the Millicell-ERS.
Submerge the probe in 75% ethanol for 15 minutes.
Remove medium from the basal compartment of the cornea-chip.
Add 100 μL of PBS to both apical and basal compartments of the cornea-chip.
Prepare a blank sterilized microdevice without cells and inject PBS into upper and lower culture channels.
Set the function switch to “Ohms”.
Remove the probe from 75% ethanol and drip it off the electrode tips.
Wash the electrode tips in PBS.
Insert the long electrode tip into the “TEER zone”.
Lower the probe until the long electrode tip touches the bottom of the well, keeping the short electrode tip above the “Culture zone” surface.
Measure the resistance on the blank microdevice and record the value (Rblank).
Measure the resistance on the cornea-chip and record the value (Rtotal).
Remove PBS from both apical and basal compartments.
Reconnect the microdevice to the low-pressure syringe pump.
Perfuse the lower channels with mixed culture medium at a volumetric flow rate of 100 μL/h.
Incubate the system at 37°C, in a 5% CO2 incubator.
Measure trans-epithelial electrical resistance (TEER) values of the corneal epithelium at specified intervals.
Wash the probe with 75% ethanol and PBS between readings if different media conditions are present.
Perform TEER measurement ideally within 5–10 minutes to ensure optimal integrity of cultures.
Incubate cells with Hank's balanced salt solution (HBSS) to equilibrate for 20 min in the incubator.
Replace HBSS with 100 μL of 100 μg/mL fluorescently labeled dextran (FITC-dextran).
Aspirate out the FITC-dextran solution from the lower compartment and refresh with 100 μL HBSS.
Collect 20 μL samples from the basal side at time 0 and 60 min.
Prepare a calibration curve of serial dilution ranging from 0.39 to 100 μg/mL FITC-dextran.
Measure the fluorescence intensity of FITC-dextran using a hybrid multi-mode microplate reader with excitation/emission wavelengths set at 488/525 nm.
Plot a graph with fluorescence intensity as the dependent variable (Y-axis) and known concentration of FITC-dextran as the independent variable (X-axis).
Prepare a blank device as a control.
Subtract the data from the blank device from all readings before analysis.

Calculate the permeability coefficient (Papp) using: P a p p = d Q / d t × 1 A C 0 where, dQ/dt is the slope of the cumulative fraction absorbed versus time, A is the area of the culture zone, and C0 is the initial concentration in the apical chamber.
Remove the stratified corneal epithelium from the PDMS device for further processing.
Add 1 mL of 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) to fix the membrane for 30 minutes.
Rinse the membrane with PBS three times gently.
Incubate in PBS at 4°C for 12 hours.
Place the membrane in 70%, then 80%, and finally 95% ethanol each for 30 minutes, followed by two rounds of 100% ethanol for 45 minutes to dehydrate the tissue.
Incubate with xylene for 30 minutes to make the tissue transparent.
Incubate in a mixture of molten paraffin wax at 56°C for 30 minutes and then in 100% molten wax for another 60 minutes twice.
Embed the membrane, section it into slices of 3 μm thickness.
Deparaffinize the sections first with a clearing agent and rehydrate from high-to-low concentration ethanol.
Rinse the slides with distilled water for 1 hour.
Immerse sections in the hematoxylin for 1 min.
Remove the rack to a beaker with tap water.
Exchange tap water until the water is clear.
Immerse sections in the eosin for 40 s.
Remove rack to a beaker with tap water.
Exchange tap water until the water is clear.
Rinse slides with 95% ethanol twice for 1 min each.
Rinse slides with 100% ethanol for 1 min.
Clear slides in the clearing agent for 1 min.
Mount coverslip onto the section on the glass slide.
Immunofluorescence staining of specific corneal epithelium protein and intercellular junctions
Incubate the membrane in 4% PFA for 30 minutes at 22°C.
Rinse with ice-cold PBS three times gently.
Place the membrane on glass slides.
Draw a circle around the membrane with a histochemical pen to prevent solution flow away.
Add 0.25% Triton X-100 for 10 minutes at 22°C.
Wash cells in PBS three times for 5 minutes each.
Block by 1% BSA for 1 hour.
Dilute the primary cytokeratin 3 antibody in antibody diluent at a 1/100 dilution.
Incubate cells in the diluted primary cytokeratin 3 antibody in a humidified chamber for 12 hours at 4°C.
Decant the solution and wash the cells three times with PBS, 5 minutes each.
Dilute the secondary Cy5-conjugated goat anti-mouse IgG antibody in antibody diluent at a 1/200 dilution.
Incubate cells with the diluted secondary Cy5-conjugated goat anti-mouse IgG antibody for 1 hour at 22°C in the dark.
Decant the secondary antibody solution and wash the cells three times with PBS, 5 minutes each in the dark.
Dilute the primary ZO1 antibody in antibody diluent at a 1/500 dilution.
Incubate cells in the diluted primary ZO1 antibody in a humidified chamber for 12 hours at 4°C.
Decant the solution and wash the cells three times with PBS, 5 minutes each.
Incubate cells with diluted secondary FITC conjugated goat anti-rabbit IgG antibody for 1 hour at 22°C in the dark.
Decant the secondary antibody solution.
Wash the cells three times with PBS for 5 minutes each in the dark.
Incubate cells with 2 mg/mL 4′, 6′-diamidino-2-phenylindole hydrochloride (DAPI) for 10 minutes at 22°C in the dark to stain the nucleus.
Add coverslip with fluorescent mounting medium for 5 minutes in the dark.
Photograph the cells with a Zeiss Axio Observer fluorescent microscope.
